subject: VPC hosting constraints & procurement checkpoints
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@regthera.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: VPC hosting constraints & procurement checkpoints

Alex — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps we agreed on. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain / goals you shared:
- Data residency: PHI must remain in Regula's US-only VPC.
- Network lockdown: no outbound internet egress from the inference nodes; only inbound control channel via customer-managed bastion.
- Auditability: 7 years of access logs, and tight KMS integration required.

Technical constraints we captured:
- Private deployment preferred (on your AWS account).
- Host-level egress policy + VPC endpoints only.
- Minimum recommended instance family: g5/hip, but we discussed mixed CPU/GPU for preprocessing.

Action items / owners:
- Regula: share basic network diagram and procurement timeline (Alex) — requested: by EOD Thu 7/15.
- Redwood SE: confirm agent connection (bastion) pattern and outbound control port list (Karthik) — delivery by Mon 7/19.
- Redwood AE: provide commercial path (SOW template, estimated committed capacity pricing) (Ben) — draft by Fri 7/16.

Attachments: I attached the minimal network sketch we used in the call (network-drawing.png) and a stub note on SOC 2 access patterns (SOC2_Access_Notes_stub.pdf).

Open questions we should resolve on the next call:
1) Will Regula accept a read-only CloudWatch/S3 access role for submission of logs to your audit bucket, or do you require push-based signed bundles?
2) Procurement timing — is there a preferred MSLA or do you need our standard MSA with two redlines?

Next meeting: propose Tue 7/20 10:00am PT for technical dive + procurement. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Thanks — jasmine

--

Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 16:32:47 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC hosting constraints & procurement checkpoints

Jasmine — thanks for the tidy recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Network diagram: attaching the preliminary topology we use internally (see attached). We'll mark the private subnets and the allowed transit gateway rules.
- Logs: procurement prefers push-based signed bundles (S3 signed uploads) for the time being. We can evaluate read-only role later in the engagement.
- Procurement timeline: Clara (cc) will own the process. We are targeting a Q3 procurement window; tentative go/no-go decision by end of July.

Procurement asks from our legal/commercial team:
1) A short SOW that limits scope to the private deployment and includes explicit data residency wording.
2) An SLA appendix covering uptime and incident response for the dedicated GPU pool.

Clara — please confirm whether we should expect a vendor questionnaire next week (I think legal will send one).

One more ask for Redwood SE: can you confirm what outbound ports the agent needs to reach Redwood control plane (if any)? We need that to freeze firewall rules.

Alex

--
Alex Mercer
Head of IT, Regula Therapeutics
alex.mercer@regthera.com | +1 (650) 555-0110
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@regthera.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC hosting constraints & procurement checkpoints

Alex / Clara — quick technical reply to the open items so procurement has the specifics for firewall/procurement: 

- Agent control plane: for private deployments we can operate in a fully customer-controlled VPC with a lightweight outbound TLS control channel (egress to a narrow set of IPs/hostnames) OR a fully air-gapped pattern where we run a local controller and we exchange signed bundles (S3). Since you require zero egress from inference nodes, the signed-bundle approach is the default.
- Signed bundles: we will provide a signed upload agent that writes to your pre-signed S3 endpoints. We supply SHA256 manifests and a verification step; we can increase retention metadata to satisfy the 7-year requirement.
- Ports/hosts: if you choose the control-plane egress route, required outbound is TLS to the following FQDNs: control01.redwood-inference.com, updates.redwood-inference.com, and metrics01.redwood-inference.com on 443. If you choose signed bundles, no outbound from inference nodes is required — only the upload host (a separate transfer job) needs egress.

Actionable next step (technical): I’ll produce a 1-page firewall whitelist vs signed-bundle playbook by Mon 7/19.

Commercial: Ben — I can sync with you on SOW language for the private deploy and the SLA appendix.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: VPC hosting constraints & procurement checkpoints

All — quick commercial note: I’ll draft a concise SOW and a short SLA appendix that maps to the committed capacity options we discussed (monthly reserved GPU pool vs. burst credits). Expect a redline-ready draft to Clara by Fri 7/16.

Clara — what cadence do you prefer for procurement checkpoints (weekly sync vs. email updates)? I can loop in our contract ops to minimize back-and-forth.

I’ll also include an optional clause for 30/60/90 day ramp pricing so you have flexibility depending on the final deployment pattern.

—Ben
